reviews.text: A graphically updated "Solar 2" with roguelite "upgrades" on new heavenly bodies you achieve. If you're going to copy an old game at least have the decency to have all the functionality of it. which includes the QoL feature of being able to spawn in as anything you previously unlocked instead of having to start from scratch. As well as, 'captured' bodies could also be absorbed via button press for resources. I do appreciate the capturing of satelites being more on purpose now. But the old system felt intuitive, - almost. "Solar 2" Is also under $5. *under $3? As of writing this review. Check it out. (Should run on toasters now.) As far as waste your time type games, that are drop in ready to play, there are worse copies in other genres. For cup o' coffee price, it's a nice coffee break type of game.

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38888018-United-Critics/] Please follow [b]United Critics[/b] for quality reviews[/url] [h2]Drifter Star: Evolution Review[/h2] [table] [th][h2]Factors[/h2][/th] [th][h2]Rating[/h2][/th] [th][h2]Description[/h2][/th] [tr] [td]🎮Gameplay[/td] [td]6.5[/td] [td]The gameplay is quite basic- dodge some objects, and collect the rest, with a bit of a room for collisions as well. [/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]📷Graphics[/td] [td]7[/td] [td]Static background but animations are good.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]🎧Narration/Audio[/td] [td]6,5[/td] [td]Alright soundtrack.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td] 😮Variety[/td] [td]6[/td] [td]The gameplay stays the same throughout- but it does get intense after each phase.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]🎰Re-playability[/td] [td]5[/td] [td]Only for the achievements.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]💲Price[/td] [td]6[/td] [td]Wait for a sale.[/td] [/tr] [/table] [hr] [h1][b]🎮 Gameplay Mechanics[/b][/h1] [table][tr][td]🔶 Drifter Star: Evolution takes you through the journey of a space body slowly turning into a black hole. The game is very simple, with collision being the only main mechanic. You start as a meteorite and move around space, collecting small rocks while avoiding heavier objects and bodies with strong gravity. Once you collect enough rocks, shown by a progress bar, you evolve into the next stage, such as an asteroid. Each time you evolve, the game lets you choose upgrades for your space body. These upgrades include things like collecting more resources or dealing more damage. In this game, resources refer to rocks or other space bodies you can absorb, depending on your current stage. For example, as a black hole, you can collect almost everything except larger black holes. Damage refers to how much a space body breaks apart when you collide with it. [/td] [/tr] [/table] [hr] [table][tr][td]🔷 When you collide with a smaller body, part of your own body breaks, but the other object completely shatters. You can then collect all the fragments, which increases your total resources. If you collide with a body of similar mass, both bodies take heavy damage but usually survive. However, colliding with a larger body instantly ends the game. The evolution stages progress in this order- Meteorite, Asteroid, Dwarf Planet, Rocky Planet, Gas Giant, Gas Planet, Dwarf Star, Star, Giant Star, Supergiant Star, Neutron Star, and finally, Black Hole. The game balances things by only placing space bodies that are within two stages above or below your current form. [/td] [/tr] [/table] [table][tr][td]🔶 Furthermore, I’d like to talk about the upgrades again. Most upgrades only last for the phase in which they are offered, unless the game clearly says otherwise. You also have the option to not pick any upgrade, which removes any extra powers for that phase. [/td] [/tr] [/table] [hr] [table][tr][td] (Only read the next part if you want to know about achievements) [spoiler] If you’re trying to collect all achievements, finishing the game without choosing any upgrades is one of them. When I tried this, a giant black hole suddenly appeared and swallowed my gas giant. I’m not sure if this happens randomly or if it’s triggered by skipping upgrades. After finishing the game five times, I didn’t really feel like testing it further. Either way, there’s an achievement for getting devoured, so it still counts. My guess is that I moved too far in one direction, which caused the black hole to spawn. So if you’re achievement hunting, try this method and also try finishing the game without selecting evolution upgrades. The remaining achievements are easy- two are earned by picking different final evolution options, and the last one unlocks when you fail for the first time. [/spoiler] [/td] [/tr] [/table] [hr] [h1][b]📝 Main Pros and Cons[/b][/h1] [b]Pros-[/b] [list] [*]Easy to understand gameplay. [*]Unique upgrades are available for each phase. [*]Visibility and animations are decent.[/list] [b]Cons-[/b] [list] [*]Content offered is quite low, that is the only major issue.[/list] [hr] [h1][b]😇 Honest Rating[/b][/h1] [table][tr][td]🔶 It’s a decent game that works well and does exactly what it sets out to do, but it clearly lacks content. While the price isn’t very high, I’d still recommend buying it on sale since the amount of content doesn’t really justify the base price. That said, it’s a nice game to relax with, especially if you play your own music in the background. [/td] [/tr] [/table] Rating: 6/10 F = GMm/r² For full review head over to our [url=https://www.united-critics.com/post/drifter-star-evolution]website[/url]

It's okay on its own. If you haven't played Solar 2, then this game might feel awesome. Whole game with everything is my 2.4 hours. It looks good, sounds decent, plays well. An improvement over Solar 2 is that in this game destroyed objects always drop "mass", they don't just evaporate. The other thing is perks: it's a cool idea, some of them work great, others feel useless or overpowered. Downgrades compared to Solar 2 are: - Lack of missions and challenges. - The interactions with other objects are forced: they just follow you around, as opposed in Solar 2 where they are randomly generated in your path as you move. - The way you get mass is by breaking objects and collect the debris, but the physics of that debris is superweird. Often other objects nearby, for no apparent reason, steal debris that is closer to you, one time I even had it just go through me into another planet. Overall all this game feels arcade-y, while Solar 2 felt like an actual universe to explore. But it's a good experience still.

[h2]Evolution starts fun but ends badly. 🌌[/h2] At first, you relax and grow your planet by eating smaller objects. But soon, the computer programming ruins the game. The enemies ignore each other. Instead, they all form a line to chase only you. 🚂 This is unfair. The computer cheats to stop you from growing. It feels like the game hates the player. You cannot use strategy to win. The game is broken, not difficult. 👎 However, the core game is too unique to throw away. I will keep the game. I hope the developers fix the AI soon.

1. 游戏的成长路线非常固定，每次升级的选项都完全一样，没有任何的随机性可言。唯一的随机性可能就是你捕获的星球，带着一群小弟去撞碎比你更大的星球。 2. 游戏玩法过于单一。你必须不停地移动，以躲避随时朝你撞过来的星球。要么它撞碎你，要么你撞碎它，然后吞掉它的一切，升级，仅此而已。与此同时，可玩区域实在是有些过于小了，根本就感觉不出宇宙的浩瀚，从开始游戏到通关，你一直在做的就是大鱼吃小鱼，躲避大星球，吃掉小星球，攒经验，升级。你必须时刻保持危机感，不停地移动，你的小弟们也得跟在你屁股后面跑，根本不能去养一个庞大的星系，因为它们会随时被朝你靠近的星球撞碎。一开始看成就里有个银河系，我以为可以一边升级，一边构建一个庞大的星系，结果并非如此，因为你压根没机会构建，因为到后期，你压根就不能捕获星球，只能将它们撞碎、吞噬，中子星、黑洞亦是如此。就算到大后期变成了黑洞，恒星、中子星们仍然会朝着你的方向飞去，然后被引力扭曲方向，最后完全吞噬。 3. 画面表现不尽人意。背景永远是单一的一张图，并且不会因为你的移动而产生任何变化。从一开始的小陨石，到最终的黑洞，这个背景是完全一样的。哪怕加点恒星撞碎了的星云也行啊。大部分时候，你甚至都感觉不到自己在移动，只有出现别的星球和小尘埃的时候才能意识到，原来自己还在移动。另外就是，两个黑洞靠近时，边上的光线扭曲效果会把另一个黑洞遮挡掉一部分，被遮挡的部分显示的是背景图，这看起来是bug而不是特效。 建议： 1. 增加可玩面积、星球种类和数量。现在的可玩空间实在是太小太小了，而且星球的种类和数量也太少太少了，真的是屈指可数，玩起来没有什么乐趣。比如可以让这些星球也拥有自己的行星、卫星，玩家可以带一队小弟，电脑也可以。增加了面积，当然也要增加数量和种类。 2. 减少过于激进的攻击。现在的玩法就是一边躲一边吃，而且越是到后期，躲就越大于吃，跟在电脑屁股后面，鹬蚌相争渔翁得利。在建议1的基础上，增加星球彼此的间距，减慢星球的移动速度，这样玩起来就会更休闲，也可以让玩家创造出一个星系来。 3. 后期和大后期的捕获能力。到了这个阶段，其实已经不需要去主动捕获了，足够强大的引力，只需要靠近就能将它们捕获。至于是养着，还是一口吞掉，那就看玩家怎么移动，这种捕获状态不再像行星、恒星的捕获那样永远绕着母星，而是受到引力的影响而改变方向，这时候玩家改变自己的位置，就能很容易地吞掉这些星球。 4. 画面的优化。背景图增加一些随机性，比如随机纹理、随机颜色等等，也可以增加一些纵深，并且可以移动，营造出一定的视差效果。就跟恒星撞碎产生星云那种效果一样，只是更加暗淡，更加遥远一些。然后随着演进，逐渐缩小。比如一开始的陨石阶段，这个背景会显得很大，很深，很浩瀚。然后这个大小一点点缩小，最终到黑洞阶段时，就会比陨石阶段小很多，也近很多。

DO NOT PLAY! It is a cool idea, broken by no idea how mass or physics works. The core identity of the game is gathering matter to make yourself bigger. The only safe way to do that is to only go after things smaller than you. Every stage of evolution just ends up being you running away from everything bigger than you slowly picking up scraps, because surprise surprise! Even as a star, if you hit another star thats the same size as you, enough times to destroy it, you somehow end up with less mass than when you started the attack. This is not how this works, and it ruins the feel of the game. By the time you reach star level attacking another star is pointless, all you do is run away from the one that can 2 shot you. Its dumb, not balanced, do not waste your $ on this game.

打着宇宙探索的幌子，实际是一个大鱼吃小鱼的游戏，升级解锁的星球没有体现出来各种星球的特色，比如说陨石坠入气态行星也会撞击撞散，小行星升级变气态行星也比较抽象，岩石行星确实有概率变成恒星，从红矮星阶段开始，游戏难度骤升，红矮星开始，就有大哥追着你，不能再考虑偷吃了，自己是恒星的时候无法把其他恒星撞成好看的星云，各种星球的引力也不对，有大哥在附近的时候，即使你离你的饲料更近，也会被大哥吃掉，同等级也会被吃掉；游戏到终局的时候一瞬间就结束了，也不给无线模式爽一下；最后发展出星系的时候，其实也挺好看的，但是也没有给时间欣赏，立马返回主菜单了，不推荐购买；纯粹是一个幌子游戏；考虑到游戏价格，还行吧，原价略亏，打折闭眼入吧
